subproblem.title: Boundary rectifiability for finite-mass integer multiplicity currents in ℝ^P
subproblem.statement: Assume DeformationTheorem (Simon 5.3) and IntegralityOfWeakLimits (Simon 8.2), as frozen. Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let X ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with M(X) < ∞ and M(∂X) < ∞. Then ∂X ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) is an integer multiplicity current.
subproblem.lean_statement: DeformationTheorem → IntegralityOfWeakLimits → ∀ (P m : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity X → X.mass < ∞ → X.boundary.mass < ∞ → IsIntegerMultiplicity X.boundary
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 4 and 5 of the parent proof (the printed proof of 6.3 for U = ℝ^P and finite masses: approximation by integer polyhedral chains, ∂P_k integer multiplicity cycles of bounded mass converging weakly to ∂X, and compactness for cycles, Remark 6.4: 8.2 for m ≥ 1, the case n = 0 for m = 0). `DeformationTheorem` and `IntegralityOfWeakLimits` are hypotheses of this statement; they are discharged by the sibling nodes root.deformation-a1 and root.integrality_weak_limits-a1 in the parent's assembly.

1. (Approximation.) By the sibling lattice_approximation (using `DeformationTheorem`) there are ρ_k > 0, β_k : `LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) P` → ℤ and Pk ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with `IsLatticeChain ρ_k β_k Pk`, Pk ⇀ X, and Λ := sup_kM(∂Pk) < ∞.
2. (Integer multiplicity of the boundaries.) Y_k := ∂Pk ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity for every k, by the sibling lattice_boundary_im.
3. (Weak convergence.) For ω ∈ D^m(ℝ^P), Y_k(ω) = Pk(dω) → X(dω) = ∂X(ω) (SimonGMT `WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary`), i.e. Y_k ⇀ ∂X.
4. (Mass bounds.) For every W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(Y_k) ≤ M_{ℝ^P}(Y_k) = M(Y_k) ≤ Λ (`massOn_mono`), so sup_kM_W(Y_k) ≤ Λ < ∞.
5. (Case m = 0.) Y_k ∈ D₀(ℝ^P) are integer multiplicity, sup_kM_W(Y_k) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P, and Y_k ⇀ ∂X in the open set ℝ^P; by the sibling zero_dim_weak_limit (with U = ℝ^P), ∂X is integer multiplicity.
6. (Case m = m′ + 1.) ∂Y_k = ∂∂Pk = 0 (`boundary_boundary`, d∘d = 0). The zero current is integer multiplicity: 0 = τ(∅,0,0) and the empty triple satisfies all conditions (∅ is null and countably rectifiable; the remaining conditions are vacuous). Hence each Y_k ∈ D_{m′+1}(ℝ^P) satisfies `IsIntegralCurrent` (Y_k and ∂Y_k are integer multiplicity). Since M_W(0) = 0 (the supremum of the values 0), sup_k(M_W(Y_k) + M_W(∂Y_k)) = sup_kM_W(Y_k) ≤ Λ < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P. As Y_k ⇀ ∂X, `IntegralityOfWeakLimits` (applied with P, m′, U = ℝ^P) shows that ∂X is integer multiplicity.
proof_key_steps: lattice_approximation: integer lattice chains P_k ⇀ X with sup_k M(∂P_k) < ∞.
lattice_boundary_im: each ∂P_k is integer multiplicity; ∂∂P_k = 0 is integer multiplicity.
∂P_k ⇀ ∂X with uniformly bounded masses on every W.
m = 0: zero_dim_weak_limit; m ≥ 1: IntegralityOfWeakLimits applied to the integral cycles ∂P_k gives ∂X integer multiplicity.
